answer: The delta multiplier is published, charged in beacon, and atlas lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2610 identities would post 3470 proofs and burn roughly 33 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
